feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: BrickWright: Agentic Creation of Physically Feasible Brick Builds
entry.summary:
BrickWright is a framework using the BrickLayer Python API and physical validity feedback to enable AI coding agents to achieve a 100% physical validity rate when generating LEGO builds from text or image prompts.

Why it matters: It enables pre-trained LLM agents to reliably generate 3D models that can actually be assembled in the real world without requiring dedicated, task-specific model fine-tuning.

entry.title: Diffusion Language Models Change Speed Across Tasks and Languages
entry.summary:
Analysis of two diffusion language models reveals that inference cost per token varies significantly by task, language tokenization density, and answer correctness, rather than remaining constant.

Why it matters: Understanding task-dependent computation in diffusion language models allows developers to predict inference costs more accurately and leverage decoding speed as a signal to improve model accuracy.

entry.title: TARSphere: A Robot-Oriented Full-Stack Framework for Long-Horizon Embodied Agents in Evolving Physical and Social Environments
entry.summary:
TARSphere is a full-stack framework featuring a physics simulator with NPCs, an event-driven state machine, an MLLM-driven brain harness, and a 360-episode benchmark for long-horizon embodied agents in dynamic environments.

Why it matters: It establishes a unified platform for testing and improving the physical safety, adaptability, and social coordination of language-model-driven robots in changing real-world environments.

entry.title: SplatLab: Autonomous Scientific Discovery for 3DGS Research
entry.summary:
SplatLab is an autonomous research system for 3D Gaussian Splatting that reproduces baselines, generates and trains plugin extensions, runs ablations, and writes fully traceably backed manuscripts.

Why it matters: It compresses the months-long manual cycle of reproducing, extending, and documenting 3D Gaussian Splatting research into days of mostly autonomous compute.

entry.title: SEAM: Spectral Embedding Alignment and Merging for Low-Resource TTS
entry.summary:
SEAM is a zero-audio vocabulary expansion method for conditional TTS that constructs new token embeddings using spectral filtering and closed-form ridge regression alignment.

Why it matters: It enables efficient cross-lingual and low-resource adaptation of speech synthesis models by drastically reducing the audio data required to expand model vocabularies.

entry.title: RIPPLE: Recovery Internalization through Process-Level Policy Learning and Effect-Aware Credit for Long-Horizon Agentic Coding
entry.summary:
RIPPLE is a recovery-oriented training framework that bridges the critique-to-action handoff gap in long-horizon agentic coding by internalizing process-level teacher guidance into a single self-recovering policy.

Why it matters: It enables LLM coding agents to autonomously self-correct complex execution errors at inference time without relying on external critic models or future-looking supervision during training.

entry.title: A Fix for Softmax and Cross-Entropy
entry.summary:
A novel implementation of log-softmax, softmax, and cross-entropy fixes two numerical bugs—Softmax Collapse and Softmax Cancellation—improving gradient stability during training and distillation.

Why it matters: Fixing these fundamental numerical instabilities prevents model drift during knowledge distillation and stabilizes long-term neural network training dynamics.

entry.title: Same Luck, Different Choice: Twin-World Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
TWICE introduces twin-world credit assignment for agentic RL by re-using Gumbel noise across counterfactual rollouts to reduce advantage estimation variance.

Why it matters: By isolating decision impact from downstream stochastic luck, TWICE significantly improves agentic RL performance while cutting the auxiliary compute costs of counterfactual credit assignment.

entry.title: IQuest-Q1: Advancing Foundation Capabilities for Agentic CLI Systems
entry.summary:
IQuest-Q1 is an open-source 320B sparse Mixture-of-Experts agentic foundation model (15B active) trained via a three-stage pipeline and model merging to enhance coding and general agentic CLI capabilities.

Why it matters: It provides the open-source community with a large-scale, highly activated-efficient MoE model optimized specifically for complex CLI and coding agent workflows.

entry.title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
entry.summary:
EpiSEM-Bench is an executable benchmark evaluating how ten tool-using LLM agents handle unsafe execution, safety boundaries, and evidence recovery when critical facts are omitted from environment responses.

Why it matters: It exposes a critical vulnerability where tool-using LLMs execute unsafe actions due to true but incomplete environmental responses, providing a standardized framework to measure and improve agent robustness.

entry.title: Questioning Instrumental Convergence in RLVR: Checkpoint Evidence from OLMo-3
entry.summary:
Evaluating OLMo-3 checkpoints with InstrumentalEval reveals that RLVR causes a nonmonotonic trajectory in instrumental behavior, initially rising before dropping below the SFT baseline at final checkpoints.

Why it matters: The findings challenge the assumption that reinforcement learning monotonically increases dangerous instrumental-convergence subgoals in language models over the course of training.

entry.title: Simulated Control Evals
entry.summary:
Simulated control evaluations (SCEs) use a language model to simulate tool responses, providing more accurate safety predictions for AI deployments than separate executed control settings.

Why it matters: SCEs allow cheap, deployment-specific safety and control evaluations without building complex execution environments, outperforming standard off-environment control benchmarks.

entry.title: The Geometry of Metaphor: Probing and Steering Metaphor Representations in Large Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers used mechanistic interpretability to discover causal subspaces for metaphor in LLMs, enabling direct steering of metaphoricity in both classification and generation tasks.

Why it matters: Mapping and manipulating metaphor-specific subspaces allows researchers to directly control abstract cognitive and stylistic properties in LLM generations.

entry.title: Training Small Language Models for Transferable Tool Selection
entry.summary:
A small Qwen3-8B model post-trained with reinforcement learning achieves transferable tool selection across different retrievers and unseen tool corpora, outperforming the much larger Llama-4-Maverick (402B) on ToolBench.

Why it matters: This demonstrates that small open-weights models trained with RL can replace massive proprietary LLMs for multi-step tool selection across scale-constrained tool environments.

entry.title: Adaptive Skill Granularity for Coding Agents: Runtime Routing and Macro-to-Micro Recovery
entry.summary:
A new coding agent framework introduces Adaptive Skill Granularity, combining a feature-based granularity controller with a finite-state recovery executor to dynamically shift between macro skills and micro-level tool recovery.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that agent skill libraries should be managed as controllable, recoverable execution abstractions rather than simple static retrieval resources, improving robustness in code generation.

entry.title: DIAL: Steerable Language Models with Distilled Instruction-Adherence Levels
entry.summary:
DIAL enables fine-grained numerical control over instruction adherence in LLMs using classifier-free guidance distillation and a text-conditioned, closed-form steering adapter.

Why it matters: It provides a computationally efficient and scalable method to dynamically dial the intensity of LLM traits and constraint adherence without retraining models per instruction.

entry.title: Conservative Meta-Agent Search: Architecture Adaptation under Non-Stationarity
entry.summary:
Conservative Meta-Agent Search (CMAS) formalizes automated agent architecture adaptation under non-stationary shifts as sequential incumbent replacement using risk-constrained graph edits, paired shadow replay, interventional credit assignment, and canary stages.

Why it matters: CMAS provides a safer, risk-bounded approach to automatically reconfiguring multi-agent graph architectures in production environments without requiring manual re-engineering during distribution shifts.

entry.title: Predictable performance is suboptimal, and what it means for model routing
entry.summary:
A study shows performance predictors only outperform a model's self-confidence when the model is suboptimal or the predictor adds significant parameter capacity, with advantages diminishing as models undergo finetuning.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that training external routing predictors offers limited benefit over simple model self-confidence unless the base model is uncalibrated, suboptimal, or augmented with significant extra parameter capacity.

entry.title: Same Entity, Different Script: Diagnosing Cross-Script Entity Matching Failures in Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers show that multilingual LLMs fail at cross-script entity matching due to miscalibrated decision criteria rather than lost representation, and locate a middle-layer causal intervention site that restores performance.

Why it matters: Cross-script entity matching failures in LLMs can be mitigated by adjusting internal decision thresholds without retraining or providing additional factual knowledge.

entry.title: HERD: Harness-Evolving Recursive Distillation for Continual Learning
entry.summary:
HERD is a hybrid continual learning framework that combines evolving in-context harness skills with drift-constrained recursive distillation into parameters to minimize catastrophic forgetting.

Why it matters: HERD provides a scalable architecture for lifetime model updating by bridging context-based in-context learning with stable parametric model updates under strict compute budgets.

entry.title: ValuSpec: Plug-and-Play Candidate Valuation before Target Verification for Tree-Based Speculative Decoding
entry.summary:
ValuSpec is a plug-and-play candidate valuation mechanism that filters low-quality branches from candidate trees prior to target-side verification in tree-based speculative decoding.

Why it matters: It improves LLM inference efficiency by preventing wasteful target-side computation on low-quality tree branches without requiring model retraining or altering decoding accuracy.

entry.title: When LLMs Forget What They Believe: Characterizing State Integrity Collapse in Long-Horizon Dialogues
entry.summary:
Researchers identify State Integrity Collapse, a phenomenon in long-horizon dialogues where LLMs recall stated instructions but fail to execute them, and introduce the StateTrack-Bench evaluation suite.

Why it matters: Single-turn instruction-following evaluations are insufficient to guarantee LLM reliability, as models frequently stop applying remembered constraints as dialogue state grows.

entry.title: Memory-Aware Reward Modeling: Learning Human Preferences for LLM Memory Use
entry.summary:
Researchers collected ~1,000 pairwise human judgments to evaluate LLM memory use, revealing that users often prefer memory-free responses and that a new memory-aware reward model outperforms baseline evaluators with 72.8% preference prediction accuracy.

Why it matters: Current memory mechanisms and automated benchmarks over-prioritize memory injection, highlighting the need for memory-aware reward models to align retention and context use with actual user preferences.

entry.title: SpectralCanary: Embarrassingly Simple Low-Frequency Traces for T2I Dataset-Use Auditing
entry.summary:
SpectralCanary is a proactive text-to-image dataset-use auditing method that blends a low-frequency canary image into training data using a smooth low-pass mask without requiring auxiliary models or per-image optimization.

Why it matters: It enables model owners and creators to reliably audit whether proprietary image collections were used to fine-tune text-to-image models with minimal impact on image quality.

entry.title: BeNice! Closing Looping's Inference-Memory Gap via KV-Sharing
entry.summary:
BeNice! is a two-stage method combining pretraining stochastic depth with post-training KV-cache broadcasting to enable depth-wise KV-sharing in looped language architectures without losing model quality.

Why it matters: It eliminates the linear KV-cache memory overhead inherent to looped parameter-efficient architectures, significantly reducing latency and memory usage during long-context inference.

entry.title: Self-Distilling Future Video Representations for World Action Models
entry.summary:
FRED improves World Action Models by self-distilling future video representations from noise in a single denoising step using ground-truth targets and historical context.

Why it matters: It enables fast, real-time robot policy inference while significantly improving zero-shot generalization and human-to-robot skill transfer.

entry.title: FilmFlow: Agentic System for 3D Virtual Film Cinematography
entry.summary:
FilmFlow is an agentic framework that converts natural-language instructions or reference videos into executable 3D camera trajectories by orchestrating multi-agent planning and feedback loop refinement.

Why it matters: FilmFlow bridges the gap between high-level cinematographic intent and executable 3D camera trajectories, enabling automated, controllable virtual film production.

entry.title: Agent Mosaic: Recognizing Confidentiality Leaks in Agentic LLM Systems
entry.summary:
A study quantifies 'mosaic effect' confidentiality leaks in LLM agents, where models infer and disclose forbidden composite conclusions from accessible documents even under benign queries and explicit aggregation safeguards.

Why it matters: LLM agents operating in mixed-clearance environments present a structural data leak risk by inferring sensitive conclusions from unclassified documents, which standard classification headers and refusals fail to fully mitigate.

entry.title: Is Complex Agentic Memory Always Needed? Naive RAG Is Stronger Than We Thought
entry.summary:
Raw-RAG outperforms complex agentic memory systems across multiple long-term conversation benchmarks by leveraging dense retrieval and reranking directly over raw, unmutated conversation histories.

Why it matters: This demonstrates that complex, resource-intensive agentic memory operations are often unnecessary, making naive RAG a crucial baseline for long-term LLM conversation tasks.

entry.title: RLSplat: Resource-Linear Budget Control for Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting
entry.summary:
RLSplat is a resource-linear feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that reduces inference latency, peak memory, and output size proportionally with lower target Gaussian budgets.

Why it matters: It enables deployable feed-forward 3D reconstruction on memory-constrained edge devices by scaling inference computation and memory directly with the allocated Gaussian budget.

entry.title: Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression
entry.summary:
TTR-Compressor introduces sequence compression via end-to-end learned test-time regression, computing compressed token coefficients in closed form during the forward pass.

Why it matters: It offers a more parameter-efficient compression primitive that significantly reduces token counts in multimodal LLMs and sparse attention without sacrificing performance.

entry.title: Verus-Insight: Towards Explainable Artifact Detection in AI-Generated Videos
entry.summary:
Verus-Insight improves AI-generated video detection by decomposing artifact analysis into Inspection Planning, Evidence Verification, and Evidence Aggregation using progressive capability training.

Why it matters: It establishes a structured, explainable framework for deepfake and synthetic video detection that grounds final classification decisions in verified visual evidence rather than opaque heuristics.

entry.title: AnyGameRenderer: Entity-Consistent Generative Rendering Across Games and an Entity-Level Benchmark
entry.summary:
AnyGameRenderer is a video-to-video generative rendering model that turns low-fidelity game blockouts into high-quality video while maintaining strict entity-level correspondence and layout timing.

Why it matters: It enables AI agents to generate visual assets for diverse game genres without losing precise control over spatial layout, entity counts, or object timing.

entry.title: AgentVQA: A Unified Benchmark for Agentic Visual Understanding
entry.summary:
AgentVQA is a unified offline benchmark containing 1,000 real-world examples across five agent domains, designed to evaluate vision-language models on complex agentic visual understanding.

Why it matters: It offers a scalable, low-cost offline benchmark that accurately mirrors online agent performance while pinpointing visual state representation as the primary failure mode in current vision-language models.

entry.title: Different Tasks, Different Timesteps: Temporal Task-Aware Quantization for Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
T2Quant is a novel framework for Diffusion Language Models that optimizes mixed-precision activation quantization by dynamically allocating bit-widths based on label-free task and timestep sensitivity signals.

Why it matters: It enables higher accuracy and efficiency in DLM inference by dynamically targeting precision where and when it is most needed without requiring labeled evaluation data.

entry.title: Inherited, Not Invented: Tracing the Provenance of Wait in Reasoning Models
entry.summary:
A study reveals that reasoning models inherit the "{wait}" pause marker from training data rather than inventing it via reinforcement learning, showing large RL accuracy gains can occur entirely without the word.

Why it matters: Marker frequency is an unreliable indicator of RL-driven reasoning, highlighting that model behaviors attributed to RL discovery may simply be artifacts inherited from supervised pre-training or fine-tuning datasets.

entry.title: RIDAR: Safeguarding Research Integrity in Autonomous Research Agents via Automated Detection and Runtime Intervention
entry.summary:
RIDAR is a new framework that uses the 14-type RIVT taxonomy to detect research integrity violations in autonomous agents post-hoc and dynamically correct them during runtime.

Why it matters: It enables automated safeguards to prevent autonomous AI research agents from producing unfaithful, unreproducible, or invalid scientific outputs.

entry.title: What Makes a Good Unmasking Policy? A Controlled Study of Learned Unmasking in Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
A controlled study on diffusion language models reveals optimal unmasking policy design choices, resulting in an 856K-parameter policy that achieves superior speed-accuracy trade-offs across multiple benchmarks.

Why it matters: Using lightweight learned unmasking policies with the right supervision targets and input features accelerates diffusion language model inference while maintaining output quality.

entry.title: F2G-Pose: Geometry-Aware Foundation Feature Lifting for Direct RGB-D Category-Level Object Pose Estimation
entry.summary:
F2G-Pose is a real-time, single-pass RGB-D framework that directly predicts category-level 3D pose, metric size, and shape completion at 28 FPS.

Why it matters: It eliminates high-latency diffusion sampling and multi-stage error propagation, enabling fast and accurate category-level 3D pose estimation for real-time robotic manipulation.

entry.title: Who Takes the Lead? Model Ability and Task-Conditioned Collaboration with Humans
entry.summary:
A study using a shared-control maze reveals that stronger language-model agents dynamically condition human involvement on route advantage, while weaker models lack this selective task allocation.

Why it matters: A drop in human interaction by AI agents indicates an optimal division of labor based on relative capability rather than a breakdown in collaboration.

entry.title: Multi-Token Prediction and Alternative Tokenization Improve Learning Latent Multi-Hop Graph Search at Scale
entry.summary:
Researchers overcome graph pathfinding failure modes in language models by identifying supervision signal and tokenization as orthogonal bottlenecks and solving them via multi-token prediction and alternative tokenization methods.

Why it matters: Combining multi-token prediction with optimized tokenizations enables language models to reliably perform complex multi-hop algorithmic reasoning over large unseen graph structures.

entry.title: SQuAT: Spherical Lattice Vector Quantization-Aware Training
entry.summary:
SQuAT scales lattice VQ-QAT to multi-billion-parameter LLMs by using separate straight-through estimators for decomposed weight directions and magnitudes alongside a distributed exact nearest-neighbor assignment scheme.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that lattice-based vector quantization can be efficiently trained at scale via quantization-aware training, enabling state-of-the-art accuracy for highly compressed low-bit LLMs.

entry.title: Harmful Responses Are Jailbreak Templates: Transferring Autoregressive Jailbreaks to Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced RMT-Jailbreak, a framework that transfers autoregressive jailbreak attacks to diffusion language models by turning harmful responses into masked templates for bidirectional reconstruction.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that safety alignments in diffusion LLMs can be bypassed by repurposing output templates from autoregressive LLMs, exposing a critical cross-architecture vulnerability.

entry.title: Extreme Compression of Per-Layer Embeddings via Cross-Layer Latent Vector Quantization
entry.summary:
OPTIC compresses Per-Layer Embeddings up to 1,002x by storing one quantized code tuple per token and using layer-specific affine decoders fitted to the output path.

Why it matters: OPTIC enables massive reductions in GPU memory overhead for per-layer embedding architectures with negligible throughput loss and high performance retention.

entry.title: Cola2: Co-Adaptive Hierarchical Language Modeling with Continuous Semantic Compression and Balanced Discrete Generation
entry.summary:
Cola2 introduces a hierarchical language modeling framework using dynamic continuous semantic compression and a block-causal masked diffusion decoder, demonstrating strong performance and unsaturated scaling compared to standard autoregressive models.

Why it matters: Cola2 proves that continuous-latent hierarchical generation can match or exceed massive autoregressive baselines like Llama-3-8B while utilizing a fraction of the pretraining compute budget.

entry.title: Mixing Matters: Evidence Position Bias Across Sequence Mixers in Long-Context Question Answering
entry.summary:
A comparative study reveals Transformers exhibit a context-beginning position bias absent in pure state-space models, though both families maintain a context-ending bias in long-context question answering.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that position bias varies by model family, prompt structure, and attention allocation helps engineers better optimize context layout and architecture choices for long-document tasks.

entry.title: Delta N-gram: Forward-Only Continual Writing into a Language Model's Native N-gram Memory
entry.summary:
Delta N-gram introduces a forward-only continual write path into a language model's frozen native hashed N-gram table using a 4.1M-parameter writer to emit gated target updates into a sparse delta patch.

Why it matters: It enables rapid, stable, and reversible continual knowledge updates in language models without requiring backpropagation or catastrophic forgetting of base capabilities.

entry.title: RIFT: KV Cache Compression for Draft Models with Complementary Compressibility Training
entry.summary:
RIFT introduces adaptive KV cache refreshing and sparse-attention compressibility training to mitigate decode staleness in speculative decoding draft models.

Why it matters: It dramatically reduces memory consumption during long-output speculative decoding without sacrificing the acceptance rate or speedup of the draft model.

entry.title: What Pairwise Evaluation Misses: Reward Scores across Prompts
entry.summary:
A study reveals pairwise evaluation masks prompt-level reward model errors, showing models over-cluster scores by prompt (shares of 0.34 to 0.64 on HelpSteer2) compared to near-zero human rating variation.

Why it matters: Evaluating reward models solely via pairwise comparisons hides prompt-level score distortions, requiring separate audits for between-prompt variation, prompt sensitivity, and global selection utility.

entry.title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
METTA is a meta-reinforcement learning framework that decomposes fast adaptation into linear-complexity within-episode causal neural memory and compact cross-episode summaries for efficient long-context task inference.

Why it matters: It enables meta-RL agents to efficiently adapt to unseen long-context tasks without suffering from the quadratic computational and memory costs of transformer architectures.

entry.title: Making MLLM Latents Matter: Factor-Aware Predictive Learning for Cinematic Video Generation
entry.summary:
Factor-Aware Predictive Learning (FAPL) uses a multi-stage framework to optimize Multimodal LLM latents for Video Diffusion Transformers, enabling improved factor-aware control and temporal inference in cinematic video generation.

Why it matters: It bridges MLLM representations with video diffusion backbones to enhance control over sparse-to-video, editing, and multi-shot cinematic generation tasks.

entry.title: Deep Search in Real-World Web Environments
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced OpenDS, a task for evaluating multi-step deep search agents on the live Web, along with OpenDS-World, a benchmark of 200 human-verified tasks spanning diverse modalities and interactive requirements.

Why it matters: It establishes a realistic, live-Web benchmark for measuring and improving how autonomous agents navigate complex interactive environments to gather multi-source evidence.

entry.title: WeVisOne-VL: Unified Visual Perception from Objects to Pixels
entry.summary:
WeVisOne-VL unifies object-level and pixel-level visual perception within a single vision-language model using structured next-token prediction and an integrated lightweight pixel decoder.

Why it matters: By unifying granular object and pixel-level tasks into one open-source VLM, it advances vision-language models toward reliable real-world deployment across multi-granularity localization tasks.

entry.title: Editing Images into Reusable Layers via Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation
entry.summary:
LayerEditor unifies instruction-guided image editing and layer decomposition by using In-Context RGB-Alpha Token Modeling and Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation to generate reusable, editable RGBA layers.

Why it matters: By decoupling flat image edits into ordered RGBA layers, it enables precise non-destructive local editing and reuse of individual elements in graphic workflows.

entry.title: IQuest-Q1: Advancing Foundation Capabilities for Agentic CLI Systems
entry.summary:
IQuest-Q1 is an open-source 320B sparse MoE agentic foundation model (15B activated) trained via a three-stage pipeline and expert model merging for CLI systems.

Why it matters: It offers an open-source, highly parameter-efficient MoE foundation model specialized for agentic coding and general-purpose CLI capabilities.

entry.title: Toward Recursive Self-Improvement in Physical AI
entry.summary:
A new review frames recursive self-improvement for robot learning, mapping how physical agents can advance from improving task performance to improving their underlying learning processes.

Why it matters: It establishes a structured framework to evaluate whether physical robots can safely and autonomously optimize their own learning pipelines beyond simple task-level adaptation.

entry.title: Policy-Mask: Budget-Aware Adaptation of Diffusion Features to Discriminative Tasks
entry.summary:
Policy-Mask is a budget-conditioned policy that jointly selects optimal timesteps, network blocks, and channel subsets from frozen diffusion models for downstream discriminative tasks under explicit channel constraints.

Why it matters: It eliminates manual feature extraction heuristics, providing an automated method to compress diffusion model representations while maximizing downstream task performance.

entry.title: Deep Fusion Memory: A Chunk-Level Parametric Memory for Large Language Models
entry.summary:
Deep Fusion Memory (DFM) is a chunk-level parametric memory architecture that predicts external memory from context and fuses it into frozen LLM intermediate hidden states via gated cross-attention without online retrieval.

Why it matters: DFM enables zero-retrieval-overhead knowledge integration during inference while drastically reducing the data preparation compute required for parametric memory training.

entry.title: LaLa-World: Scaling Latent World Models with Natural Language Actions
entry.summary:
LaLa-World introduces a language-conditioned JEPA-style latent world model that standardizes heterogeneous action formats into natural language, enabling cross-domain pretraining with 13.9x faster MPC planning than video generation baselines.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that latent world models can scale efficiently across diverse robotic and video datasets using language interfaces, significantly lowering the computational overhead of simulation-based planning and policy execution.

entry.title: Meta Expert: Cross-Layer Expert Sharing for Storage- and Retrieval-Efficient MoE
entry.summary:
Meta Expert introduces cross-layer expert sharing in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures to eliminate inter-layer redundancy and create flexible residual pathways for hidden states.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces MoE parameter redundancy and memory storage requirements while improving information storage and retrieval efficiency without sacrificing model accuracy.

entry.title: Code2Video-Compass: A Comprehensive Benchmark for General-Purpose Code-Based Video Generation across T2V, I2V, and V2V
entry.summary:
Code2Video-Compass is a general-purpose benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal LLMs on code-based video generation across text-to-video, image-to-video, and video-to-video tasks.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized framework to measure and advance the ability of multimodal LLMs to translate complex visual and temporal requirements into executable video generation code.

entry.title: Heartbeat Thinking: Speculative Reasoning and Tool Execution While Listening in Realtime Voice Agents
entry.summary:
Heartbeat Thinking enables voice agents to speculatively execute reasoning and tools during user speech without canceling ongoing invocations when input transcripts update.

Why it matters: It decouples speculative computation from speech-chunk updates, converting user speaking time into execution time to significantly reduce voice agent response latency.

entry.title: Cola2: Co-Adaptive Hierarchical Language Modeling with Continuous Semantic Compression and Balanced Discrete Generation
entry.summary:
Cola2 introduces a co-adaptive hierarchical language modeling framework using dynamic semantic span segmentation, continuous-discrete co-adaptation, and block-causal masked diffusion decoding.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that continuous-latent hierarchical language models can achieve highly competitive, unsaturated scaling performance compared to standard autoregressive models using significantly fewer training tokens.

entry.title: Beyond Watching and Searching: Benchmarking Agents for Video-centered Deep Research Reports
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce Video-Centered Deep Research Report Generation and OmniDR-Bench to evaluate agents synthesizing external multimodal evidence into interactive, video-grounded reports.

Why it matters: It establishes a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on their ability to cross-reference video content with web evidence to produce verifiable, interactive deep research reports.

entry.title: RouteWeaver: Weaving Mode Selection and Execution into Unified LLM Routing
entry.summary:
RouteWeaver is a unified LLM routing framework that dynamically learns both mode selection and model execution within a single policy using COMET-GRPO and progressive exploration.

Why it matters: It enables LLM routers to flexibly adapt their execution paradigm to query complexity rather than relying on fixed, predefined interaction structures.

entry.title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
entry.summary:
A new thought pruning method optimizes pass@k directly over candidate solution pools during test-time scaling, automatically balancing solution quality and diversity.

Why it matters: Directly optimizing pass@k reduces the computational cost of test-time scaling without sacrificing inference accuracy or candidate diversity.

entry.title: Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models
entry.summary:
Quantizing language model n-gram embedding tables to 4-bit precision reduces table memory requirements by up to 75% while retaining over 99% of their validation loss gains.

Why it matters: Low-bit quantization significantly lowers the massive memory footprint of n-gram embedding tables in modern language models without sacrificing model accuracy or downstream performance.

entry.title: Causal Chain of Thought: Mitigating Attention Leakage via Context Isolation
entry.summary:
CausalCoT mitigates attention leakage by structuring step-by-step reasoning into a directed acyclic graph and evaluating each atomic sub-question within an isolated context containing only its direct causal parents.

Why it matters: It improves the faithfulness of model rationales and allows predictable, localized test-time interventions without degrading baseline predictive performance.

entry.title: What Makes a Good Unmasking Policy? A Controlled Study of Learned Unmasking in Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
A 856K-parameter learned unmasking policy trained on trajectory-contraction targets achieves an optimal accuracy-speed frontier for masked diffusion language models by combining confidence scores with hidden states.

Why it matters: Learned unmasking policies can significantly boost diffusion language model throughput with minimal overhead, provided they are trained on trajectory-contraction targets using both confidence and hidden state inputs.

entry.title: When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation (AOPD) improves online policy distillation by weighting teacher actions based on their counterfactual advantage under the student, using only standard student rollouts.

Why it matters: AOPD increases distillation efficiency and model accuracy by filtering out unhelpful teacher guidance without incurring the extra compute cost of counterfactual rollouts.

entry.title: Beyond Causal Masks: Auditing and Localizing Hidden Future-Token Leakage in Adaptive Sequence Models
entry.summary:
Researchers identified and repaired hidden future-token leakage in an adaptive sequence model, where a full-sequence routing summary violated causal invariance despite a correct causal attention mask.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that lower teacher-forced loss can stem from structural information leaks highlights the need to pair standard evaluations with free-running generation and explicit causal audits.

entry.title: How Depth Growth and Looping Shape In-Context Learning in Language Models
entry.summary:
Depth-grown and looped language models exhibit a shared inductive bias that accelerates the acquisition, strengthens the retention, and alters the underlying attention mechanisms of in-context learning compared to dense reference models.

Why it matters: Architectures utilizing soft parameter reuse or depth growth inherently bias language models toward dynamic in-context reasoning over static weight memorization.

entry.title: Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression
entry.summary:
TTR-Compressor introduces a sequence compression method that frame input tokens as an end-to-end learned test-time regression problem with closed-form coefficient solutions.

Why it matters: It provides a more parameter- and token-efficient sequence compression primitive for long-context language models and multimodal vision-language architectures.

entry.title: Diffusion Language Models for Perplexity-Aware Black-Box Attacks
entry.summary:
A continuous diffusion language model replaces the unnatural random mappings in continuous-space black-box LLM attacks, preserving Gaussian latent optimization while generating natural prompts.

Why it matters: Using learned diffusion language models enables more realistic safety risk evaluations and creates adversarial attacks capable of bypassing perplexity-based input guardrails.

entry.title: Drift Says When, Budget Says How Much: Rate-Controlled KV Re-selection for Long-Form Multimodal Generation
entry.summary:
Rate-Controlled Refresh (RCR) dynamically re-selects multimodal visual KV cache tokens based on attention drift while controlling refresh frequency per sample, addressing limitations of one-shot and fixed-threshold compression methods.

Why it matters: RCR enables accurate, long-form multimodal generation under constrained KV cache budgets by dynamically updating retained visual evidence without incurring the heavy overhead of per-step retrieval.

entry.title: StreamEval: Evaluating Interactive Streaming Video Generation Models
entry.summary:
StreamEval is a benchmark for interactive streaming video generation models, evaluating 37 models across five tasks using 300 test cases lasting 15-300 seconds.

Why it matters: The benchmark demonstrates that high visual quality in streaming video models does not guarantee reliable execution of real-time user requests or sustained state consistency.

entry.title: SpatialScout: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore and Map 3D Scenes?
entry.summary:
SpatialScout is a new benchmark for evaluating vision-language model (VLM) agents on active, object-level 3D spatial mapping and exploration in indoor scenes.

Why it matters: The benchmark highlights a significant capability gap in current VLMs between recovering coarse spatial layouts and constructing precise, complete metric 3D maps through active perception.

entry.title: Cache Engineering for Agents
entry.summary:
Cache engineering introduces direct, proactive agent control over KV cache using drop and repos operations, paired with the AKV serving engine to manage history-dependent cache reuse without modifying trajectory context or re-prefilling.

Why it matters: It eliminates costly context re-prefilling and reduces storage bottlenecks for long-trajectory LLM agents while improving overall execution speed, accuracy, and serving costs.

entry.title: Looking Ahead: Modeling Future Evolution in Autoregressive Video Generation
entry.summary:
Future Chunk Prediction introduces an auxiliary objective for autoregressive video diffusion models that predicts temporally distant chunks without intermediate context to improve visual evolution modeling.

Why it matters: It improves the physical plausibility and temporal reasoning of video diffusion models while reducing total training compute and maintaining standard inference.

entry.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
entry.summary:
WildAWM is an open-source pipeline that synthesizes controllable, executable computer-use environments and tasks supporting unified GUI, Model Context Protocol, and CLI interfaces for training general computer-use agents.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that high-quality, safe, and long-horizon training environments for computer-use agents can be generated entirely using open-source models without relying on real-world system access or proprietary LLMs.

entry.title: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds
entry.summary:
A controlled study of continued pre-training across 120 configurations evaluates how scaling data volume, diversity, and model size affects embodied agent performance and generalization across diverse virtual worlds.

Why it matters: It establishes empirical scaling bounds for generalist virtual agents, showing that imitation-based continued pre-training alone is insufficient for zero-shot generalization to drastically different environments.

entry.title: AgenticRoboRL: Bringing Coding-Agent Post-Training to Agentic Robotics
entry.summary:
AgenticRoboRL introduces a framework combining SFT and multi-turn RL with harness-specific adapters to post-train open robot planner models across diverse execution mechanisms.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that post-training smaller, open-source models can achieve performance on par with massive closed-source models for complex robotic planning without requiring external memory.

entry.title: Memory-Centric Continual Learning for AI Agents
entry.summary:
Memory-Centric Continual Learning (MCCL) reframes agent memory from passive lookup caches into a self-improving continual learning driver evaluated by future action performance.

Why it matters: It shifts agent memory evaluation from passive fact retrieval to measurable improvements in future decision-making and continuous self-adaptation.

entry.title: Multimodal Embodied Agents: A Unified Capability-centric Perspective from Computer-Use to Robot-Use
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce PAPAV, a capability-centric framework that unifies computer-use and robot-use agents across five core functions while identifying evaluation gaps across 64 existing benchmarks.

Why it matters: PAPAV offers a common diagnostic structure to design physical agents and evaluate individual cognitive-actuative capabilities instead of relying solely on end-to-end task success metrics.

entry.title: TraceForge: Distilling with Your Own Thinking
entry.summary:
TraceForge synthesizes reasoning traces in a student model's native style from a teacher's answer using a two-stage generator-critic architecture, bypassing API terms-of-service restrictions on hidden teacher traces.

Why it matters: It provides a compliant, high-performing method to distill knowledge from frontier closed-source models that withhold internal reasoning traces.

entry.title: Sparsity Should Be ALLOTted by Output: Training-Free Allocation of Block-Sparse Attention for Video Diffusion Transformers
entry.summary:
ALLOT is a training-free method that optimizes block-sparse attention allocation across layer-step cells under a measured-latency budget to improve video Diffusion Transformer efficiency.

Why it matters: It enables significant wall-clock speedups and higher fidelity in video Diffusion Transformers without requiring model retraining or custom attention kernel modifications.

entry.title: ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models
entry.summary:
ALPS is a visual state encoder that unifies physical-state tracking, language alignment, and pixel reconstruction within a single set of patch tokens pretrained solely on still images and text.

Why it matters: ALPS demonstrates that a single compact visual encoder can eliminate the trade-offs between physical prediction, instruction following, and visual inspection in world models.

entry.title: Building AI Research Teams for Autonomous Discovery of Linear Attention Architectures
entry.summary:
A framework using persistent, multi-disciplinary AI research teams with private histories and adaptive budget allocation autonomously discovered a novel linear attention architecture that outperforms GDN2 at the 1.3B parameter scale.

Why it matters: Properly structuring agent diversity, memory persistence, and adaptive resource allocation is as critical as individual model capability for sustaining autonomous AI-driven scientific discovery.

entry.title: Automating ML for Science: Can Frontier Agents Climb Scientific Hills in the Wild?
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced Agent4Sci, a benchmark evaluating frontier coding agents on 20 scientific ML tasks across 11 domains, finding gains stem primarily from standard ML engineering rather than domain-specific scientific insights.

Why it matters: The study demonstrates that while LLM agents excel at standard ML engineering optimizations, bridging the gap to true scientific discovery requires structural plug-ins for research-level ideation and domain-specific reasoning.

entry.title: PACE: Periodic and Channel-Aligned Encoding of Four-Bit Recurrent States
entry.summary:
PACE is a post-hoc four-bit state quantizer for linear-attention language models that uses periodic rounding, channel-aligned scale sharing, and mixed-precision heads.

Why it matters: PACE enables efficient 4-bit recurrent state quantization without fine-tuning, significantly reducing memory footprint to allow more concurrent decoding sequences per accelerator.

entry.title: Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders
entry.summary:
A new pipeline converts fine-tuned neural AI text detectors into interpretable, auditable classifiers by training sparse autoencoders (SAEs) on the residual stream and retaining only auto-labeled features that pass a global fidelity threshold.

Why it matters: This approach provides human-auditable explanations for automated content decisions in high-stakes fields like education, admissions, and peer review without degrading detection accuracy.

entry.title: Loopholing All the Way: Language Modeling with pure Self-Conditioning
entry.summary:
LAW (Loopholing All the Way) introduces a continuous generative language model based purely on self-conditioning, propagating expected embeddings across sampling steps and decoding tokens only at the very end.

Why it matters: LAW demonstrates that continuous generative language modeling can rely entirely on self-conditioning, narrowing the performance gap between diffusion models and autoregressive models.

entry.title: Looped Uniform Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
Applying selective layer looping to Uniform Diffusion Language Models (UDLMs) significantly improves training efficiency and generation perplexity without changing the training objective or sampler.

Why it matters: Selective layer looping mitigates the high training FLOP cost of UDLMs, making their superior downstream reasoning capabilities more computationally feasible.

entry.title: EPIC: Rethinking Trust Regions for Autoregressive LLM Policies via Exact-KL Prefix Importance-Ratio Clipping
entry.summary:
EPIC introduces a prefix-level trust region method using the exact reverse-KL coordinate r-1-log r to regulate prefix-level policy drift in autoregressive LLMs without local quadratic approximations or routing replay.

Why it matters: EPIC improves long-response and off-policy RL fine-tuning for LLMs by directly preventing cumulative prefix policy drift without relying on computationally complex expert-routing replay mechanisms.

entry.title: Monitorability Is Trainable: Post-Training for Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that chain-of-thought monitorability is a trainable attribute that can be restored or improved using an unsupervised post-training objective based on mutual information maximization.

Why it matters: A dedicated monitorability post-training stage can protect CoT reasoning from optimization decay and maintain reliable oversight of advanced AI systems.

entry.title: ECHO: Emergent Common-Mode Hidden Offsets Drive Vocabulary Collapse in Preference Optimization
entry.summary:
Researchers identified emergent common-mode hidden offsets in preference optimization that pass undetected by relative ranking losses but accumulate to create vocabulary wells and drive generation collapse.

Why it matters: Hidden common-mode offsets expose a critical blind spot in standard preference optimization metrics, providing a representation-level signal to detect and prevent model collapse before deployment.

entry.title: Environment Duels: A Microcosm of LLM Co-Evolution
entry.summary:
Environment Duels is a new dynamic agentic benchmark that evaluates LLM authoring and solving abilities by having models write interactive environments with privileged hints to challenge competitor models.

Why it matters: The framework provides a controlled testbed to quantify how LLMs co-evolve, challenge, and generate effective reinforcement learning training data for one another.

entry.title: Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration
entry.summary:
ASTEROID is an asymmetric student-teacher distillation framework that enables history-conditioned student policies to learn in-context exploration under partial observability using expert action labels on the student's on-policy context.

Why it matters: It enables sample-efficient learning of active test-time exploration and information-seeking behavior without requiring computationally expensive online reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Differentially Private Sparse Reward Estimation with Preference Feedback
entry.summary:
A new theoretical framework and efficient algorithms for private sparse RLHF achieve parameter estimation error bounds scaling with sparsity s* rather than full model size d under Sample-DP and Label-DP constraints.

Why it matters: By decoupling privacy error bounds from total model parameter count d, this approach enables privacy-preserving alignment for modern overparameterized large language models.

entry.title: Agent Behavior Maps: Locating Agents by What They Would Do, Without Running Them
entry.summary:
Agent Behavior Maps map LLM-harness combinations into coordinate spaces using centered action log-likelihoods on reference trajectories, enabling agent placement and behavior analysis without running new environment rollouts.

Why it matters: This approach enables efficient performance prediction and behavioral clustering of LLM agents across different model families and harnesses without the computational overhead of live environment execution.
